title: A `.novis/completion` folder anywhere in the workspace holds JSON files of values the editor offers at the string parameters they name, and nothing in them is run
scope:
The `.novis` folder as a project's place for data its tools read, the `completion` kind inside it, the format of a
completion file, and how the language server finds, reloads, checks and offers one, with the VS Code client's part
(the file watcher and a JSON schema). Any other kind of content under `.novis`, and any reader other than the language
server, are left to the record that adds one.
dependsOnText:
[0108](0108.md) (its § 2, the terms on which a value enters a completion list, which this record widens),
[0240](0240.md) (a string argument mapped to its parameter through `crate::arguments`, and `'` and `"` as trigger
characters answered only inside a string the editor completes).

summary.headline: A project can add its own completion values for any string parameter
summary.body:
Put JSON files in a `.novis/completion/` folder anywhere in your project. Each file lists values and the method
parameters they belong to. When you type a string at one of those parameters, the editor offers the values. Each
value can have a label, an icon, a title and a Markdown description. You can write the files by hand, or generate
them with any script, for example from a dataset or an icon set. The editor reloads a file when it changes. The
files are only read and never run.
